primitives.name: Event-ID Keyed Game Row Retrieval
primitives.verbatim_quote: ESPN public scoreboard fetched by date and keyed by **event id**, never by team-and-time (team-and-time is the field a duplicate-fixture defect corrupts, so matching on it would hide the defect being measured).
primitives.assumptions: Game rows are uniquely identifiable by event ID; team-and-time fields are subject to duplication defects.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When team-and-time is used for matching, duplicate fixtures mask corruption.

layer2.mapping: The event ID provides a stable isomorphism between internal game state and external ESPN data, enabling accurate comparison and detection of corruption.
layer2.telemetry: Mismatch rate between internal game rows and ESPN final scores.

primitives.name: Settlement Contradiction Detector
primitives.verbatim_quote: Why this was necessary The settlement-contradiction detector compares a stored result against what the **game row** implies.
primitives.assumptions: Stored results are compared against the implied outcome of the game row; agreement indicates consistency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Detects when a pick agrees with a corrupted game row, returning CONSISTENT even if incorrect.

layer2.mapping: Kernel of consistency checking derived from game row validity; blind spot arises when row itself is corrupted.
layer2.telemetry: Number of picks marked CONSISTENT despite being graded against corrupted rows.

primitives.name: True Final Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: Sports covered: MLB 491, NFL 66, MLS 62, NCAAF 51.
primitives.assumptions: External alignment with ESPN provides ground truth for final scores across sports domains.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Incomplete fetches (e.g., 104 missing event IDs) limit full coverage.

layer2.mapping: ESPN final scores act as a shared reference frame for validating internal game outcomes across all sports.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of correctly aligned picks per sport category.

The settlement-contradiction detector fails when a pick is graded against a corrupted row because it only compares against the row’s implication, not its truth. True final alignment with ESPN allows detection of such inconsistencies. The failure mode lies in the structural blind spot where a corrupted row appears consistent internally. This leads to misclassification of picks as correct when they are not. The telemetry for this includes mismatch rates across sports, especially MLB where 62/438 moneylines were wrong. The retrocausal genealogy traces back to early data ingestion models that relied on unstable identifiers. Agents involved include the ingestion system, the settlement engine, and the external ESPN feed. Anti-collinearity is ensured by using distinct identifiers and cross-validating against independent sources.
